items.title: The Cheapest Stocks in the S&P 500: Are They a Bargain or a Trap?
items.summary: Inflation is stubbornly high, but not in home broadband service.  There, telecom operators are making fiberoptic inroads in a business long dominated by cable television companies.  The result has been discounting:  UBS  reports that prices for various broadband service tiers are down 7% to 14% for fiber over the past year, and 17% to 27% for cable.

items.title: Are You Overpaying For Verizon Stock Versus Its Rivals?
items.summary: A $10,000 stake in Verizon Communications (VZ) a year ago is now worth about $11,660, the top result in its group of five. Verizon ranks only third of the five on revenue growth and third again on operating margin. So are you paying for what Verizon earns today, or for a recovery it has only started to show.

items.title: An 8-Day Losing Streak Has Charter Communications Stock Down 20%
items.summary: Charter Communications (CHTR) stock has now moved lower for 8 consecutive trading days, a cumulative loss of 20%. That streak has erased about $3.5 billion from the company's market value, which now stands at about $14 billion. For anyone holding the stock, the persistent selling has pushed the price to a new low for the year.

items.title: Is Comcast Broken, Or Just Paying To Defend Its Broadband?
items.summary: Comcast (CMCSA) shares sit about 43% below their two-year high, a price that looks like a bet the business is shrinking. Yet over the past twelve months Comcast generated nearly $18 billion of free cash flow, a yield of 22.2% on its market value against 4.5% for the median S&P 500 company. Which reading is right? It turns on a choice Comcast made more than a year ago: lower broadband prices to hold customers against new rivals.

items.title: Charter Communications (CHTR) Eyes Cable Deals With CFO Pushing A Disciplined Approach
items.summary: Charter Communications (NasdaqGS:CHTR) is evaluating potential cable sector acquisitions as part of its current corporate agenda. The firm's CFO has highlighted a disciplined merger framework that prioritises financial prudence and balance sheet resilience. Management has indicated that any transaction would need to align with existing capital allocation plans and leverage targets.
